direct: Attackers changed temperature settings at a Slovenian meat plant, setting a freezer chamber to 100°C and locking a technician out; staff prevented damage and disconnected all cooling systems from the network (stated). Similar cases were reported the same days at a Bern butcher, Swiss Volg branches and an Italian supermarket, where technicians said they had about thirty similar problems (stated).
downstream: Food spoilage, recalls and store closures if a change goes unnoticed, as at the Bern butcher that closed temporarily (stated for Bern; wider effect is an inference).

More attempts against internet-reachable refrigeration and building controllers across Europe while default accounts remain (inference; Danfoss AK-SM 800A flaws are in CISA KEV, but no source names the brand in these incidents).
watch_for: A national CERT advisory naming the controller product used in these incidents
Reports from more retail chains or cold-storage operators
Scanning reports for refrigeration controller web interfaces
who_should_care: Supermarkets, butchers, food processors and cold-chain logistics
Refrigeration and HVAC service contractors who manage controllers remotely

direct: Drupal says core access bypass CVE-2026-136716 (SA-CORE-2026-019) is exploited in the wild, a week after the exploited installer flaw SA-CORE-2026-017.
downstream: Drupal says sites whose installer stayed reachable after 017 may already be compromised, so updating does not clean a site that was taken over (stated).
Government, university and media sites run Drupal widely; defacement, data theft or use as phishing hosts are likely follow-ons (inference).
watch_for: A CISA KEV entry for CVE-2026-136716
Unexpected admin accounts or a reinstalled site
Mass-scanning reports for install.php and the 019 path
who_should_care: Drupal site owners and hosting providers
Public-sector web teams

direct: A vulnerability in PLAID's KARTE platform was exploited on Nov 13; customer firms keep publishing counts, now including Peach Aviation (up to about 9.44 million records), New Balance Japan (up to about 3.74 million), Shueisha, Athenia and Kokubu.
downstream: Peach's case, per ITmedia, involved data PLAID still held after the contract ended, which puts supplier data-retention terms in question (stated for Peach).
Phishing in Japanese naming the affected brands, using leaked names, birth dates and contact details (inference).
watch_for: Further customer notices and revised counts
A regulator (PPC) statement on PLAID
Brand-impersonation phishing citing the KARTE leak
who_should_care: KARTE customers and other Japanese SaaS buyers
Customers of the named brands

direct: SAP confirmed suspicious activity and says it found no evidence so far of access to customer business data; Der Spiegel reports stolen employee tokens let attackers copy and modify source code in SAP's GitHub environment (reported, not confirmed by SAP).
downstream: If source code was modified, customers would need assurance that shipped code and build pipelines were not altered (inference).
Attackers with SAP source code can look for flaws faster, so later SAP patches may be reverse-engineered more quickly (inference).
watch_for: SAP's account of what repositories were accessed and whether any code was changed
Out-of-band SAP security notes
Phishing that uses the incident to target SAP customers
who_should_care: SAP customers and SAP security teams
Any organisation using GitHub with long-lived employee tokens

direct: Switzerland's BACS says five attacks used AI agents; four compromised systems and three targets were critical-infrastructure operators (SRF names electricity, water and telecoms).
downstream: Agencies now confirm agent-run intrusions against infrastructure, not only researchers; time from exposure to compromise shrinks (stated by BACS in urging fast patching; scale is an inference).
Other national CERTs are likely to publish similar counts (inference).
watch_for: BACS details on the flaws used
Similar statements from other European agencies
Reports of agent-driven scanning bursts against utilities
who_should_care: Energy, water and telecom operators
SMEs with internet-facing systems and slow patch cycles

direct: Binance says about $6.34 billion was affected and about $2.85 billion frozen or intercepted; the FBI attributes the theft to North Korea's TraderTraitor. Reuters reports more than $600 million laundered through THORChain.
downstream: Regulators cite the theft: the UK FCA reportedly presses ahead with DeFi authorization rules (stated).
Pressure on THORChain and coinjoin services, and on exchanges that receive their outputs (inference).
watch_for: Further US forfeiture filings
Exchange freezes of laundered funds
More fake-job coding tests aimed at crypto engineers
who_should_care: Exchanges, bridges and DeFi protocols
Crypto firms' engineering and hiring teams

direct: Reuters, citing anonymous sources, reports hackers breached the US Air Force's Cloud One platform, reportedly reaching its control plane through a software flaw; NBC says a US official confirmed the breach. Scope and attacker are unknown.
downstream: Workloads and contractors hosted on Cloud One may need credential and access reviews (inference).
Adds to a week of reported US national-security system intrusions; no link stated (timing only).
watch_for: Air Force or DoD statement on scope
Which software flaw was used and whether it is in commercial products
Advisories to defence contractors
who_should_care: US defence contractors and DoD cloud tenants
Teams running cloud control planes

direct: South Korea's PIPC activated an emergency response after 1,019 breach reports in January to October 2026 against 447 in all of 2025, with three months of inspection support from December.
downstream: Inspections and penalties for firms with weak controls; more breach notices as checks begin (inference).
Korean users face phishing using data from Korea Post, Olive Young, banks and others leaked this week (inference).
watch_for: PIPC inspection findings and fines
Further disclosures from financial firms such as E9Pay
Korean-language smishing using leaked delivery data
who_should_care: Organisations processing personal data in Korea
Korean financial and logistics firms

direct: The UK DWP took some online services offline after identifying what its secretary called a serious cyber incident; the NCSC is investigating and the government says there is no evidence of customer data loss so far.
downstream: Benefit claimants may face delays in online services while systems are restored (inference; DWP says regular payments continue).
Scammers often impersonate an agency during its outage (inference).
watch_for: DWP and NCSC updates on cause
Phishing posing as DWP or Universal Credit
Any ransomware claim naming DWP or a supplier
who_should_care: UK public-sector bodies and their IT suppliers
Benefit advice organisations

direct: Palo Alto Networks says PAN-OS management interfaces were compromised through PHP2Shell then Fragnesia (CVE-2026-46300).
downstream: Firewalls with exposed management planes may be backdoored even after patching (inference).
Check Point and Palo Alto management planes under attack in the same weeks; no shared actor stated.
watch_for: Vendor indicators of compromise
Wiper activity on gateways
KEV deadlines
who_should_care: Network security teams running PAN-OS or Check Point
MSSPs managing firewalls
